title: Finite tame sheaves over a universal residual SNC neighborhood
statement:
Let $k$ have characteristic a positive prime $p$, let $V=\operatorname{Spec}B$ be regular Noetherian and separated of finite type over $k$, and let $t_1,\ldots,t_r\in B$ cut out a strict normal crossings boundary [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary]. Put $J=(t_1,\ldots,t_r)$, assume $S=\operatorname{Spec}(B/J)$ nonempty and connected, and put $V^\circ=\operatorname{Spec}B[1/(t_1\cdots t_r)]$. Let $B\to H$ be obtained by henselizing $(B,J)$ [lem-weil-pbc-pair-henselization] and taking the filtered colimit of finite etale lifts of all pointed connected finite etale Galois covers of $S$ [thm-weil-pbc-finite-etale-lifting, lem-sfb-pointed-finite-etale-limit-cover]. Assume compatible primitive roots of all orders prime to $p$ are fixed in $H$, with distinct-root differences units. Put $U^\circ=\operatorname{Spec}H[1/(t_1\cdots t_r)]$, $T^\circ=\varprojlim_{(n,p)=1}\operatorname{Spec}(H[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/(x_i^n-t_i)_i)[1/(t_1\cdots t_r)]$, and $G=(\prod_{q\ne p}\mathbf Z_q)^r$, with $q$ running over primes, acting by the chosen root rotations. Profinite products $X[P]$ mean inverse limits of finite disjoint unions [def-sfb-profinite-test-objects].

Let $\mathcal C$ be the full subcategory of sheaves of finite sets on $U^\circ_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] obtained by pulling back finite locally constant sheaves on $V^\circ_{\mathrm{proet}}$ that become constant on every punctured strict-local full prime-to-$p$ parameter-root tower. Locally constant finite means locally isomorphic, on a pro-etale cover, to the constant sheaf of a finite set. A punctured strict-local tower uses the strict henselization [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization] and the boundary parameters at that geometric point; at points on fewer components only the vanishing parameters are used. Choose a geometric point of $T^\circ$ [def-weil-geometric-point]. Evaluation there, with root-cover monodromy, is a fully faithful functor from $\mathcal C$ to finite discrete continuous $G$-sets. For each $F\in\mathcal C$ with fibre $Q$, there is an isomorphism
$$F|_{T^\circ}\cong\underline Q_{T^\circ}$$
whose deck descent arrow on $T^\circ[G]$ is $(x,g,v)\mapsto(x,g,g\cdot v)$, in the convention that the torsor comparison sends $(x,g)$ to $(x,gx)$. These isomorphisms are natural in all maps of finite sheaves and respect finite products and the terminal object. For a finite ring $R$, they therefore carry an $R$-module sheaf to its finite $R$-module fibre with continuous $R$-linear $G$-action and respect reduction along maps of finite coefficient rings. They commute with pointed refinements of the residual cover and the charts, via the induced maps of parameter-root towers. No assertion about infinite-coefficient sheaves, inverse limits of sheaves, or extension across the boundary is included. The case $r=0$ gives constant finite sheaves and the trivial group.

source.place: Expose IX Proposition 2.1(i)–(iii) and proof, printed pp.133–134: finite tame covers and simultaneous parameter-root quotients. Residual lifting: Stacks pione.tex Tag 09ZS, lemma-gabber. Passage to limits and finite-local-system comparison: Bhatt–Scholze Corollary 5.1.5 and Lemma 7.4.3. Agent-formulated normalized finite-fibre consequence; not an infinite-coefficient extension theorem.

proof.text: Use the universal-residual-chart lemma for the identity chart and all boundary labels, with the given pointed residual system and roots. It supplies the henselian pair $(H,JH)$, the universal residual limit $\operatorname{Spec}(H/JH)$, connected nonempty finite punctured levels $X_n$, connected full tower $X=T^\circ$, and the pro-etale cover $X\to U^\circ$. These are precisely the data required below.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1(i)-(iii), printed pp.133-134, universal-residual-chart specialization; henselian residual system as in Stacks pione.tex Tag 09ZS (lemma-gabber).

proof.text: Choose $F_0$ pulling back to $F$. The finite tame root-model lemma applies to its stipulated strict-local tower trivializations and gives $n$ prime to $p$ and finite etale $E_n\to\operatorname{Spec}H_n$ representing $F|_{X_n}$. It includes the empty sheaf and imposes no restriction on the cover degree.

source.place: Bhatt-Scholze Lemmas 5.1.2 and 5.1.4, p.34; ILO IX Proposition 2.1, pp.133-134; finite-model node encapsulates returned Steps 2-3.

proof.text: Apply universal-residual root-algebra splitting to $H$, $J=(t_i)$ and the pointed limit over $S$. It splits $E_n$, hence makes $F|_{X_n}$ constant finite. Thus every $F\in\mathcal C$ lies in the category of finite sheaves trivialized at a connected finite level.

source.place: Stacks pione.tex Tag 09ZS (lemma-gabber), more-algebra.tex Tag 09XK (lemma-integral-over-henselian-pair); residual-root splitting node encapsulates returned Steps 4-6.

proof.text: The compatible Kummer Cech calculation identifies the finite overlaps with $X_n[\Gamma_n]$ and the full overlap with $X[G]$, with comparison $(x,g)\mapsto(x,gx)$ and the stated root rotations. Apply normalized connected abelian tower descent: its hypotheses are Step 1 and these comparisons. It gives the normalized splitting, the continuous left action, the exact descent arrow on the whole overlap, and full faithfulness on $\mathcal C$.

source.place: ILO IX Proposition 2.1, p.133, root rotations; Bhatt-Scholze Lemma 5.1.2, p.34; separated Cech and descent nodes encapsulate returned Steps 7-10.

proof.text: Finite products stay in $\mathcal C$: form them on the chosen $F_0$; each strict-local constant trivialization remains constant finite. By the last clause of normalized connected abelian tower descent, its category of finite-level trivialized sheaves is exactly the category of sheaves whose pullback to $X$ is constant finite, so its unique normalized splittings, their naturality and the descent formula on $X[G]$ are the hypotheses of normalized finite-splitting operations on that whole category. Apply that lemma. It gives naturality, finite products, the terminal object, finite-ring linear actions, and coefficient reduction: the sheafified $R'\otimes_RM$ is again constant finite on $X$, with its normalized tensor comparison on fibres. For pointed chart or residual refinements, the universal-chart lemma supplies maps through the fixed geometric point (choosing compatible roots of relating units); the Kummer Cech calculation makes them equivariant and preserves both projections. The pointed-refinement clause then identifies the pulled-back normalized splitting, action and entire descent arrow, compatibly with composition.

source.place: Bhatt-Scholze Section 5.1, pp.34-35, finite coefficient and pointed pullback consequence; universal residual charts and explicit root-coordinate maps.

proof.text: If $r=0$, every $H_n=H$ and $X=U^\circ$, while $G=1$. The splitting already obtained is therefore a constant splitting on $U^\circ$ itself, and all descent arrows are identities.

source.place: Empty parameter tuple specialization of returned Steps 4-7 and 12.

proof.text: Scalar-reduction companion, formally assembled in Lean: apply original-chart tame scalar closure to obtain hN. Independently construct the canonical stalk isomorphism by preservation of the neighbourhood colimit under the given left adjoint and by the sheafification-unit isomorphism at the geometric point. The latter is proved for module coefficients using Mathlib Point.ofIsCofiltered and its skyscraper adjunction; the coprojection equation follows from the two colimit comparisons. Form the R-linear sheaf map from M to restriction of N by composing the coefficient adjunction unit with the sheafification unit. Naturality and the coprojection formula identify its stalk map with unit followed by restriction of the comparison. Apply semilinear naturality of normalized stalk actions. Finally, injectivity of the coefficient adjunction hom equivalence converts its R-linear equivariance equation into the desired S-linear equivariance of the comparison. This closes the scalarReduction body; the classifier-existence and pointed-refinement bodies remain open with the original proof plans above.
